\[
\hat{F}(f) = \frac{\overline{H(f)}}{|H(f)|^2 + \gamma |P(f)|^2}\, G(f),\quad \frac{1}{N} \| g - h * \hat{f} \|^2 = \sigma^2,\quad \sigma = 5
\]

The formula shows the default parameter values.

where

- \(G, H, F\): The spectra of the blurred image, the PSF and the estimate
- \(P\): The transform of the Laplacian kernel
- \(\gamma\): The weight found from the noise level
- \(N\): The number of FFT samples
- \(\sigma\): The noise standard deviation

Constrained least squares follows Gonzalez and Woods. It minimizes the roughness |p * f|^2. The constraint is that the blurred estimate differs from the image by as much as the noise. P is the transform of the 4-neighbor Laplacian kernel p. The solution has the form of the Tikhonov filter with weight gamma. Gamma is chosen so that the mean square of the residual g - h * f, per sample of the FFT grid, equals sigma^2. Gonzalez and Woods adjust gamma step by step. This filter finds it by 60 bisection steps on log10 gamma from -10 to 4, its own search. The residual grows with gamma, so the bisection always converges. If no gamma in the range fits, the nearest end is used. The PSF is the kernel of the Gaussian filter cut at 4 sigma, of the motion blur filter, or of the disk averaging filter.
